title: Tells
summary: A co-op 1950s detective game for 1-4 players. Question suspects across the interrogation table, watch their faces through the one-way glass, and catch the lie they can't hide. Each detective files a sealed report: name the culprit and climb to Chief, or get busted down to Janitor.
about:
They all say the same thing. Only one of them is lying about it.

Tells is a first-person co-op detective game for 1 to 4 players, set in a 1950s police precinct. Every shift brings one case and three suspects in holding. Read the case files, call each suspect into the interview room, and work out who did it. Their words won't give them away. Their faces will.

READ THE FACE, NOT THE WORDS
A suspect says the same words whether they're lying or not. The lie shows on the face: a glance away, a tight jaw, a nervous habit that wasn't there a moment ago. Every suspect has tells of their own and a resting baseline to read them against. Some of those tells will show up on the truth as well.

INTERROGATE TOGETHER
One detective sits across the table and chooses the questions. The rest watch through the one-way glass. Follow a line of questioning, press on a detail, go back and ask again. If you ask twice, you'll hear "I already told you," and you can see whether the story held. Step away from the table and a squadmate can take over.

FILE YOUR OWN REPORT
When all three suspects have been questioned, each detective files a sealed report at the filing cabinet: who did it, why they did it, and every lie you caught. Reports are scored one by one. Get it right and you're promoted toward Chief. Get it wrong and you could end up mopping the precinct floors as Janitor.

FROM SMALL TIME TO THE BIG TIME
Start in the Harbor with a till short at the laundromat and a stolen car, then move up to theft, arson and worse. Each case is harder than the last: quieter tells, sharper lies, more red herrings. Close a case and tomorrow brings the next. Leave one open and it comes back with the culprit drawn again.

FEATURES
- Co-op for 1 to 4 players
- Fully voiced suspects with expressive faces and personal tells
- One case a day, three suspects, exactly one culprit
- Branching interrogations with follow-ups, callbacks and pressure
- Sealed reports scored for each player, with promotions and demotions
- A campaign of cases that grow more serious as you go
